title: Decisions and loops
subtitle: Sequence, selection, repetition: every program ever written is built from these three.

if.title: if, else if, else
if.body: if (cond) { … } else if (cond2) { … } else { … }. Only the first true branch runs. Beware = (assign) versus == (compare) inside a condition, and the “dangling else” — an else belongs to the nearest if, so use braces.

sw.title: switch
sw.body: switch (n) { case 1: …; break; case 2: …; break; default: … } jumps to the matching case. Without break control falls through to the next case — sometimes useful, often a bug. The selector must be an integer or char.

for.title: for loop
for.body: for (init; condition; update) body: init once, test before each pass, update after each pass. Use it when the number of repetitions is known. The sum of even numbers 1–10 below is 2 + 4 + 6 + 8 + 10.
for.steps: Iterations of for (i = 0; i < n; i++) when n = 10. i takes 0,1,…,9: ten passes.

while.title: while and do–while
while.body: while (cond) tests first, so may run zero times; do { … } while (cond); runs at least once. Use while when the count is unknown. break leaves a loop; continue skips to the next pass.

nest.title: Nested loops and patterns
nest.body: An outer loop of m passes containing an inner loop of n passes runs the inner body m × n times — the basis of tables, matrices and patterns (and of O(n²) cost). Triangle of stars: row i prints i stars.
nest.steps: Outer 4 passes, inner up to row number: 1 + 2 + 3 + 4. Total inner passes.
